text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
MAARIV
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu proposes former justice minister return to post now he's been acquitted in court.
- Heavy exchange of fire in south Lebanon.
- Israeli shoots dead Palestinian who tried to steal car.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Heavy exchange of fire in Lebanon.
- Former justice minister interested in returning to post; current minister says he won't give up portfolio.
- Israeli ambassador to U.S. wants Israel to protest strongly over U.S. eavesdropping on embassy.
- Magazine: President Weizman angry Netanyahu did not want to hear about his meeting with Palestinian President Arafat.
JERUSALEM POST
- Former justice minister acquitted.
- Heavy fighting in Lebanon.
- The movement to become observant of Jewish law gains adherents among the young and disadvantaged.
- Parliamentarian accuses Israel's two largest fuel companies of coordinating bids in tender to supply the defence ministry with oil.
- Insurance supervisor warns insurers not to employ cartel culprits.
- Nice to buy Canadian firm for $8 million.
- Motorola Israel plans R&D centre in Jordan to overcome shortage of software engineers in Israel; it is already advertising in Jordan for experts in software development.
HAARETZ
- Eight Israeli soldiers wounded in Lebanon.
- Former justice minister acquitted.
- Prime minister's director general initiates bill to bypass approval procedures for "national projects" like annexing land to airport.
